summary.result: The results showed that shifts in heading and maturity dates were significantly influenced by both historical climate trends and cultivar-specific traits.
summary.background: Growth stage data for four wheat cultivars-Jogwang, Uri, Keumgang, and Jokyung-were collected from the Barley and Wheat Crop Growth Information Service provided by the National Institute of Crop Science for the period 1974-2022.
summary.method: The calibrated model was then applied to simulate growth stages under varying sowing dates and historical climate conditions, enabling an analysis of the interaction between wheat growth stages and climatic factors.
